intro: Independent integer measurements add through convolution of their mass functions. Their numeric support locations matter separately from their probability arrays.
task: Convolve two finite integer-supported probability vectors and track the resulting support offset.
requirements: p and q are probability vectors on consecutive integer supports starting at start_p and start_q; starts are integers in [-10000,10000].
Return {"start": start_p+start_q, "probabilities": length len(p)+len(q)-1 mass vector} for the sum of independent measurements.
Include zero-probability bins inside the support. Independence means each pair contributes the product of its probabilities.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

examples.name: Two binary measurements
examples.output:
{'start': 0, 'probabilities': [0.25, 0.5, 0.25]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 10 significant digits.)

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: The minimum sum is the sum of the two support starts.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Accumulate each pair into output index i+j; multiple pairs can produce the same total.

explanation: Independent integer measurements add through convolution of their mass functions. Their numeric support locations matter separately from their probability arrays.
Probability mass is conserved because every pair of outcomes contributes once. The expectation of the result must equal the sum of the two input expectations, a useful independent check.
